problems.title: Menu-driven calculator
problems.question: Write a C program for menu driven addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of two given numbers.
explanation: Use switch for the selected arithmetic operation. Division by zero is rejected. Operands are bounded to keep results finite.

problems.title: Armstrong number
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to find whether a given number is Armstrong or not.
explanation: An Armstrong number equals the sum of each decimal digit raised to the number of digits. Integer multiplication avoids floating-point power rounding; zero is included.
flow: Start → read nonnegative n → count digits → reset t=n and sum=0 → repeatedly add (last digit)^digits and remove last digit → compare sum with n → print → stop.

problems.title: Greatest of three
problems.question: Write a C program to find the greatest among three given numbers.
explanation: Start with a and update the current greatest value. Equal inputs are handled.

problems.title: Matrix addition
problems.question: Write a C program to find the addition of two matrices.
explanation: Both matrices must have the same dimensions. Add matching entries; dimensions are bounded to 10×10.

problems.title: Palindrome number
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to test whether a given number is a palindrome.
explanation: Use a copy to preserve the original number. This numeric interpretation ignores leading zeros and rejects negative input.
flow: Start → read n → t=n, reverse=0 → append t%10 to reverse → t=t/10 → repeat while t>0 → compare reverse and n → print → stop.

problems.title: Quadratic roots
problems.question: Write a C program to find the roots of a quadratic equation using an else-if ladder.
explanation: The discriminant separates two real, repeated and complex roots. Handle a=0 as a linear/degenerate equation. The q formula reduces cancellation for distinct real roots. Near-zero discriminants remain subject to floating-point rounding.
For this bounded classroom implementation, nonzero coefficients must have magnitude from 10⁻⁶ through 10⁶; this avoids unrepresentable roots from tiny coefficients.

problems.title: Fibonacci up to a limit
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to print Fibonacci series up to a given number.
explanation: Interpret “up to a given number” as a maximum term value, not a count of terms. Include both occurrences of 1. The 10⁹ bound keeps addition safely inside long long.
flow: Start → read limit → a=0,b=1 → while a≤limit print a and update (a,b)=(b,a+b) using a temporary → stop.

problems.title: String length without library
problems.question: Write a C program to find string length without a library function.
explanation: Count characters until newline or the null terminator; do not count the newline. Length here counts bytes, not Unicode characters.

problems.title: Matrix multiplication
problems.question: Write a C program to multiply two matrices.
explanation: Require A columns=B rows. Compute each output entry as a row–column dot product. Bounded entries/dimensions prevent long long overflow.

problems.title: Array maximum
problems.question: Write a C program to find the maximum number in a given array.
explanation: Initialise with the first element so all-negative arrays work.

problems.title: Concatenate without library
problems.question: Write a C program to concatenate two strings without library functions.
explanation: Copy the second string after the first and append a null terminator. The destination has room for both 100-character lines. No strlen/strcat/strcpy is used.

problems.title: Linear search
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to implement linear search.
explanation: Scan left to right and return the first matching position, numbered from 1.
flow: Start → read array and target → i=0 → compare a[i] → if equal print i+1 and stop → increment i → repeat until i=n → print not found → stop.

problems.title: Perfect number
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to test whether a number is perfect.
explanation: A positive perfect number equals the sum of its proper positive divisors. For 1 the sum is zero.
flow: Start → read positive n → sum=0,d=1 → while d≤n/2 add d if it divides n → increment d → compare sum=n → print → stop.

problems.title: Binary search
problems.question: Write a C program to implement binary search.
explanation: Requires ascending sorted input; reject unsorted arrays. Each comparison halves the search interval. With duplicates, any matching position may be returned.

problems.title: Average marks using arrays
problems.question: Write a C program to find average marks for n subjects for one student using arrays.
explanation: Assume all subjects are marked out of 100. Use double division and reject zero subjects.

problems.title: Prime number
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to test whether a number is prime.
explanation: A prime is an integer greater than 1 with no divisor from 2 through √n. The test d≤n/d avoids computing d*d.
flow: Start → read n → if n<2 print not prime → otherwise try divisors d=2 while d≤n/d → if divisible print not prime → if none print prime → stop.

problems.title: Compare strings with library
problems.question: Write a C program to compare two strings using a library function.
explanation: strcmp returns a negative value, zero or a positive value. Do not assume it returns exactly −1 or 1. Comparison is case-sensitive byte order.

problems.title: Selection sort
problems.question: Write a C program to sort array elements using selection sort.
explanation: Select the smallest remaining element and swap it into the next position. Sorting is ascending; at most 100 bounded integer elements.

problems.title: Sum of 1D array
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to sum a 1D array.
explanation: Use long long for the accumulated sum. With these bounds its magnitude is at most 100 million.
flow: Start → read n and array → sum=0,i=0 → while i<n add a[i] and increment i → print sum → stop.

problems.title: Greatest using nested if–else
problems.question: Write a C program to find greatest among three numbers using nested if–else.
explanation: Nested comparisons explicitly choose between a/b first and then compare the larger one with c. Ties are valid.

problems.title: Insertion sort
problems.question: Write a C program to sort array elements using insertion sort.
explanation: Insert each element into the already sorted prefix by shifting larger elements right. Sorting is ascending; at most 100 bounded integer elements.

problems.title: Factorial
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to find factorial of a number.
explanation: 0!=1. Restrict n to 20, whose factorial fits in unsigned long long on standard-conforming implementations.
flow: Start → read 0≤n≤20 → f=1 → for i=2..n set f=f*i → print f → stop.

problems.title: Bubble sort
problems.question: Write a C program to sort array elements using bubble sort.
explanation: Swap adjacent out-of-order elements; stop early if a pass makes no swaps. Sorting is ascending; at most 100 bounded integer elements.

problems.title: Row sums
problems.question: Write a C program to find the sum of each row of a 2D array.
explanation: Reset the sum at the beginning of each row. Rectangular matrices are allowed.

problems.title: Diagonal elements
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to print diagonal elements of a 2D array.
explanation: The source does not specify which diagonal: this solution prints both diagonals of a square matrix, labelled separately. The centre appears in both lists for odd order.
flow: Start → read square matrix → for i=0..n−1 print a[i][i] → for i=0..n−1 print a[i][n−1−i] → stop.

problems.title: Star pyramid
problems.question: Write a C program to print a pyramid of * up to the given number.
explanation: Interpret the number as a row count; row i has n−i spaces and 2i−1 stars.

problems.title: String copy without library
problems.question: Write a C program to copy a string without library functions.
explanation: Copy characters through and including the null terminator. The destination holds all permitted input plus its terminator.

problems.title: Upper triangular values
problems.question: Write a C program to print upper triangular values of a 2D matrix.
explanation: For a square matrix, include the main diagonal and entries with column≥row. Blanks below the diagonal show the original positions.

problems.title: Four string library functions
problems.question: Write a C program using at least four string library functions.
explanation: Demonstrate strlen, strcpy, strcat and strcmp. Each input is at most 100 bytes, and the 202-byte destination is large enough for both plus a terminator.

problems.title: Reverse a number
problems.question: Write a C program and draw flowchart to print the reverse of a number.
explanation: This is numeric reversal of a nonnegative integer, so leading zeros of the reversed representation are discarded: 1200 becomes 21.
flow: Start → read n → reverse=0 → append n%10 → n=n/10 → repeat until n=0 → print reverse → stop.
